concern.concern: The Definition says that holonomy around either meridian is conjugate to diag(i,−i), immediately after permitting a smooth O(2)-reduced A0 in A0+(1/4)diag(i,−i)dθ. Exact finite-loop holonomy does not follow from that hypothesis. Locally, A0=c diag(i,−i)(x dy−y dx) is smooth and preserves the reduction, but changes radius-r meridional holonomy to exp(±2πi(1/4+cr²)), generally not traceless. Specify limiting meridional holonomy, or impose an appropriate exact model near the link. The primary source explicitly discusses asymptotic holonomy in Proposition 3.2's proof: https://people.math.harvard.edu/~kronheim/khovanov-unknot.pdf, printed p.29.

original_concerns.reason: The written smooth O(2)-reduced background need not be flat on a finite meridian. In the displayed abelian local test, xdy−ydx restricts to r²dtheta, so finite-radius holonomy is exp(±2pi i(1/4+cr²)); its conjugacy class need not be traceless. Smoothness instead makes the background contribution tend to zero as r tends to zero, so the limiting conjugacy class is correct. The proposed correction preserves the actual singular-residue/orbifold data. For flat connections homotopy invariance makes finite meridians conjugate to that limiting class, preserving the flat representation calculations.

required_own_edits.source_excerpt: Parallel transport (holonomy) around either meridian is conjugate in $SU(2)$ to $\operatorname{diag}(i,-i)$; its image has order two in $PU(2)$.
required_own_edits.proposed_replacement: As the radius of a meridional circle tends to zero, its holonomy conjugacy class tends to that of $\operatorname{diag}(i,-i)$ in $SU(2)$; the limiting image has order two in $PU(2)$. This is the prescribed asymptotic meridional holonomy, not an assertion of exact holonomy on every finite-radius circle for an arbitrary smooth $A_0$. For a flat connection the holonomies of homotopic meridional circles are conjugate, so their conjugacy class is exactly this limiting class.
